subject.title: Session files not being cleaned up (disk bloat)

question: Should OpenClaw define a default proactive retention policy for all stale session artifact classes in this issue, or keep cleanup split across narrower explicit commands and disk-budget pressure?
rationale: The source proves partial cleanup exists, but broader automatic deletion affects session diagnostics, recovery, and retained history semantics, and an open PR already owns the narrower deleted/reset reporting gap.

options.title: Scope Broad Cleanup Policy
options.body: Define which `.deleted.*`, `.reset.*`, `.tmp`, `.bak.*`, checkpoint, and trajectory artifacts may be removed automatically, under which retention and mode rules.

options.title: Land Narrow Reporting First
options.body: Review and land the open deleted/reset reporting PR while leaving this issue open for the remaining suffixes and proactive cleanup policy.

options.title: Split By Artifact Class
options.body: Close or narrow this broad tracker only after each remaining suffix or sidecar class has a canonical issue with clear safety semantics.

recommendation.title: Scope Broad Cleanup Policy
recommendation.body: Define which `.deleted.*`, `.reset.*`, `.tmp`, `.bak.*`, checkpoint, and trajectory artifacts may be removed automatically, under which retention and mode rules.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the cleanup UX and maintenance controls that this policy would extend.
